subject.title: feat(acp): pipe lifeline — reap the bridge tree on abrupt owner death

question: Should acpx core adopt this POSIX pipe-lifeline helper, including detached bridge process groups, lazy per-user native compilation/cache, and the ACPX_LIFELINE_HELPER override?
rationale: The code looks coherent and tested, but this is a durable runtime and packaging contract with compatibility and operational implications that automation cannot choose for maintainers.

options.title: Accept the lifeline model
options.body: Merge once a maintainer explicitly owns the native helper, lazy compile/cache behavior, fallback limits, and POSIX process-group signal semantics as core acpx behavior.

options.title: Narrow to cooperative cleanup
options.body: Ask for a smaller PR that only group-kills descendants during normal close/startup failure and leaves abrupt owner death for a separately approved native-helper design.

options.title: Pause for platform policy
options.body: Hold the PR until maintainers define whether native helpers should ship through source compilation, future platform packages, or another packaging path.

recommendation.title: Accept the lifeline model
recommendation.body: Merge once a maintainer explicitly owns the native helper, lazy compile/cache behavior, fallback limits, and POSIX process-group signal semantics as core acpx behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete most recently merged the adjacent queue-owner lifecycle repair and owns recent release/package-surface history in this area.
